summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L.5 -- Contract-Preamble and AST-Guard Relative-Import Narrow Repair. FINAL VERDICT: NARROW REPAIR IMPLEMENTED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. Same-version, contract-text-and-test-only narrow repair of exactly the three residual defects independently found by 149O.20L.7L.4. (1) HMIC-001 v1.4's top-of-document Status/Identity preamble (before section '## 0.') asserted, present tense, that a hard-coded `mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified = False` ceiling at hatp_mandatory_cutover.py:842-853 was unchanged -- 149O.20L.7L.3's own §57.9 whole-document scan had misclassified this exact paragraph historical, when it in fact restated the identical stale-current-claim defect class rows 33/34/36/37 already corrected. Independently reconstructed current production truth (src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_cutover.py lines 865-904): no hard-coded False assignment exists; Phase 149O.19.5F (Wave F) replaced it with a fresh, uncached call to validate_active_hatp_mandatory_independent_verification_certification, mapped via exact CertificationStatus.VALID identity (certification_status_satisfies_readiness), fail-closed on every other status/exception. Repaired the preamble sentence in place, same version, to name this current mechanism without overstating certification/readiness/activation status -- explicitly disclaiming HMIC certification, HATP readiness, Boundary C completion, first use, and DeploymentBinding existence (contract §58.1, new). An independent whole-document re-scan (distinct from 149O.20L.7L.3's own §57.9) for the same defect-class variants found no other live, non-archival stale-current-claim hit; §48's 'Explicit Confirmations' section and §49-57's phase-history sections remain correctly classified historical (each restates its own named phase's past-tense snapshot); HMIC-REQ-114/HMIC-REQ-075/attack row 4 remain correctly classified normative-requirement-text. (2) `_pcae_import_targets` (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_hmic_frozen_source_scope_amendment_independent_verification.py), the AST-level producer-reachability guard helper, filtered every detected import target to a pcae.-prefixed name -- but a relative ast.ImportFrom node's own `.module` is never pcae.-prefixed by itself (None for `from . import x`, or the bare intra-package name for `from .x import y` / `from ..pkg import x`), so every relative import of the DeploymentBinding producer was silently invisible. Confirmed not purely theoretical: relative imports are a live convention elsewhere in this codebase (schema_runtime/**, 29 instances independently recounted). Repaired: added `_module_name_for_path` (canonical, deterministic, Path.parts-based file-path-to-dotted-pcae-module derivation, platform-separator-independent) and `_resolve_relative_import_base` (reproduces Python's own importlib._bootstrap._resolve_name relative-import-level algorithm) to resolve every relative ImportFrom node (node.level >= 1) to its absolute dotted target before the existing absolute-import logic runs unchanged on the resolved name. Covers level-1 (`from . import x`, `from .x import y`) and multilevel (`from ..pkg import x`) forms, aliasing, single- and multi-line/parenthesized forms, and multiple imported names per statement. A relative import that climbs above the pcae package root, or that occurs in a file with no derivable module context, fails closed into the wildcard/suspicious set as a synthetic `<unresolved-relative ...>` entry -- never silently treated as 'no import found'. (3) `test_admin_script_is_the_only_non_test_caller_of_the_producer_entry_points`, a second, broader critical producer-reachability guard co-located in the same test module (scanning all of src/ + scripts/, a broader scope than the src/pcae-only AST guard), still called the un-widened `_pcae_imports` after 149O.20L.7L.3 introduced `_pcae_import_targets` and migrated only the narrower guard. Migrated in place to `_pcae_import_targets`, mirroring that earlier migration's own precedent exactly -- an actual switch of which helper inspects the import targets, not a re-scoped expected-caller list; the guard now also surfaces any wildcard/unresolved-relative hit as an unexpected-importer finding. Helper inventory at close: `_pcae_imports` (the original, absolute-only helper) is retained unmodified -- it still backs `test_producer_pair_reaches_no_unbound_pcae_module`, an unrelated completeness check over the producer pair's own outbound dependencies, not a producer-reachability guard (SAFE TO KEEP per this phase's own item 34); no other test module's own local `_pcae_imports`-style reproduction (149O.19.3/149O.19.3R eras) references the DeploymentBinding producer at all -- both predate its existence, left untouched; the 149O.20L.7L.3/149O.20L.7L.4 test modules' own historical reproductions of the pre-repair helper are deliberately preserved as regression evidence, not live guards. All three findings were independently reproduced before repair (mutation-testing disposable copies of real src/pcae module content, e.g. src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py and src/pcae/core/paths.py, with relative-import forms injected) and confirmed closed after repair. Added tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_5_contract_preamble_and_ast_guard_relative_import_narrow_repair.py (63 new tests): preamble text/citation checks, whole-document scan, byte-immutability of already-repaired rows/requirements, module-context derivation unit tests (_module_name_for_path, _resolve_relative_import_base including escape-root cases), relative-import adversarial-form detection (level 1, level 2/multilevel, alias, multiline, multi-name, wildcard), negative controls (string literal, comment, docstring, unrelated relative import), absolute-import no-regression check, five mutation tests against disposable copies of real src/pcae/core modules (level-1 bare, level-1 module-symbol, multilevel, absolute no-regression, false-positive string-literal control), second-guard-migration proof (AST-level call-name inspection), first-guard-still-repaired proof, unrelated-completeness-helper-untouched proof, remaining-blind-helper-caller inventory, whole-tree zero-producer-importer re-check, AST-based dynamic-reachability search (importlib.import_module/__import__/subprocess/Popen/runpy/os.system, scoped to Call nodes whose own source segment names the producer -- not naive same-file substring co-occurrence, which false-positived on hatp_mandatory_certification.py's own unrelated git-subprocess usage), pyproject entry-point/CLI re-check, digest/scope/production-source immutability, and no-first-use-artifact proofs. Also updated, in place, five test bodies in the 149O.20L.7L.3 and 149O.20L.7L.4 verification modules that had explicitly documented these three gaps' continued existence (each carrying its own original instruction to update rather than silently leave green/red with a now-false meaning once the gap closed, mirroring 149O.20L.7L.3's own precedent for updating 149O.20L.7L.2's finding classes): 149O.20L.7L.3's test_archival_phase_history_sections_left_untouched (removed the now-obsolete first assertion whose premise -- that the §0 preamble was archival -- 149O.20L.7L.4 disproved; kept the still-valid archival-text assertion); 149O.20L.7L.4's test_finding_section_0_preamble_still_claims_a_hardcoded_ceiling_that_does_not_exist (renamed/flipped to confirm the repair), TestFindingRelativeImportBypassRepairedHelperMisses's two tests (renamed/flipped to confirm detection, now writing scratch files into src/pcae/core/ so a real module context resolves rather than the pre-repair tempfile.mkdtemp() location, which -- correctly, post-repair -- fails closed to the wildcard set instead of an empty result), test_admin_script_only_caller_check_still_uses_the_unrepaired_helper (renamed/flipped), and test_second_guard_would_miss_a_from_import_form_by_mutation (renamed/flipped, now asserting _pcae_import_targets, the helper the guard actually uses post-migration, catches the form). Added contract §58 (Contract Repair History -- Phase 149O.20L.7L.5) documenting all three repairs, a new header 'Repaired by' line, and an updated Status line. HMIC-001 remains v1.4; HMIC-REQ-050's thirty-file enumeration and HMIC-REQ-052's three limbs unchanged; rows 33/34/36/37/38/39 and the HMIC-REQ-145 closure paragraph confirmed byte-unchanged; implementation_scope_digest recomputed live: 65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8, matching expected exactly; derive_contract_versions still returns the unchanged five-member set. git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src/pcae/ returns empty -- zero production source changed. Full raw -m fast_green suite independently re-run on this phase's own committed working tree: 254 failed, 7551 passed, 5 skipped, 9 errors -- 263 total non-passing node IDs, of the identical thematic character as 149O.20L.7L.3's own already-published raw baseline of 263 (Dell pinned-SHA drift checks, Class-B full-HBDC readiness contract integration analysis, HMIC v1.2 HBDC bound-contract-identity test-fixture errors -- all pre-existing, none touching this phase's own scope). A 263-item deselect list derived from this run produces a clean 7551 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, run twice for stability, identical both times. No DeploymentBinding producer/admin/verifier source was touched. No Dell access. No RepositoryIdentity, no DeploymentBinding, no election, no CHGR, no certification, no activation. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. F-7L-5 and F-7L-7: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. 7J section 31: remains NOT CLOSED, pending a clean 149O.20L.7L.6. Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7L.6, an independent verification of exactly this phase's own three repairs, before the 7J finding may close or first-use sequencing architecture may begin.
